row.question:
Based on the chest X-ray findings from the posteroanterior and lateral views (Fig. 1a, 1b), which of the following is the most likely description of the observed mass, and what is its clinical implication in this patient?
A) A well-defined, centrally located mass in the right upper lobe, suggesting a benign lesion.
B) An irregular, ill-defined mass in the left lower lobe extending to the mediastinum, consistent with pulmonary epithelioid haemangioendothelioma (PEH).
C) A calcified nodule in the left upper lobe, indicating granulomatous disease.
D) A solitary, round mass in the left lower lobe with sharp margins, typical of a bronchogenic carcinoma.
E) Multiple small nodules scattered throughout both lungs, suggesting metastatic disease.
F) A large pleural effusion on the left side with mediastinal shift, indicating severe congestive heart failure.

reference.correct_choice_text: An irregular, ill-defined mass in the left lower lobe extending to the mediastinum, consistent with pulmonary epithelioid haemangioendothelioma (PEH).

historical_prediction.json.raw_response:
Answer: B) An irregular, ill-defined mass in the left lower lobe extending to the mediastinum, consistent with pulmonary epithelioid haemangioendothelioma (PEH).  
Reason: The PA view (Fig. 1a) shows a large, heterogeneous opacity in the left lower lung zone with indistinct margins and mediastinal involvement; the lateral view (Fig. 1b) confirms a posteriorly located, poorly demarcated mass extending toward the hilum/mediastinum—findings characteristic of PEH, a rare vascular tumor that often presents as an ill-defined, infiltrative mass with mediastinal extension, rather than a sharply marginated nodule or effusion.

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When comparing serial CXRs showing apparent reduction of pulmonary nodules, especially in upper lobes, and clinical context suggests chronic infection or granulomatous disease
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for replacement of nodular opacities by fine linear/reticular densities without mass effect or volume loss—suggesting fibrotic scarring rather than simple regression
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Requires high-resolution images; unreliable if overpenetrated or obscured by superimposed structures

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When mediastinal opacity obscures one heart border and tracheal deviation is present on PA CXR
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect which cardiac border is silhouetted (left border loss = left mediastinal pathology; right border loss = right-sided) and confirm tracheal deviation direction—deviation away from mass side—and compare costophrenic angle blunting severity per side.
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable if both borders obscured or in severe cardiomegaly; requires adequate inspiration and centering.
